thinkers.name: Laozi
thinkers.quote: when his task is accomplished and his work done, the people all say, 'It happened to us naturally'
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — laozi, daodejing (the wu-wei, ziran, and subtraction chapters).md
thinkers.parts: It dissolves the striving self into the uncarved block; the book restores the first person.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — laozi, daodejing (the wu-wei, ziran, and subtraction chapters).md

thinkers.name: Zhuangzi
thinkers.place: Warring States China (the state of Song, by tradition)
thinkers.quote: For the perfect man employs his mind as a mirror. It grasps nothing: it refuses nothing. It receives, but does not keep
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — zhuangzi (wu-wei, the fasting of the mind, and sitting in forgetting).md
thinkers.parts: He dissolves the striving self and fixed standpoint; the book restores a sovereign first person.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — zhuangzi (wu-wei, the fasting of the mind, and sitting in forgetting).md

thinkers.name: Plato
thinkers.quote: all enquiry and all learning is but recollection
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — plato, meno and theaetetus on drawing-out and wonder (c. 380 bce).md
thinkers.parts: Recollection rests on an immortal soul's prenatal knowledge, which the book does not take.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — plato, meno and theaetetus on drawing-out and wonder (c. 380 bce).md

thinkers.name: Nāgārjuna
thinkers.quote: there is no distinction whatsoever between saṃsāra and nirvāṇa
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — nāgārjuna, mūlamadhyamakakārikā (c. 150 ce).md
thinkers.parts: He reaches 'already free' through no-self and emptiness, never through a Self to recognize.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — nāgārjuna, mūlamadhyamakakārikā (c. 150 ce).md

thinkers.name: Bhartṛhari
thinkers.quote: coloured by adventitious impurities, is not really affected by them
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — bhartṛhari's levels of speech and kṣemarāja on saṅkoca (vākyapadīya i; pratyabhijñāhṛdayam).md
thinkers.parts: He ranks the soundless above speech; the book holds the descent is not degradation.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — bhartṛhari's levels of speech and kṣemarāja on saṅkoca (vākyapadīya i; pratyabhijñāhṛdayam).md

thinkers.name: Śaṅkara
thinkers.quote: is to remove the obstructions produced by ignorance
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — brihadaranyaka upanishad 2.3.6 and shankara on neti neti.md
thinkers.parts: He uncovers an attributeless Self, negating the personal first person the book restores.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — brihadaranyaka upanishad 2.3.6 and shankara on neti neti.md

thinkers.name: Utpaladeva
thinkers.quote: though he is there before her he does not give her any pleasure until she recognizes who he is
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — the kashmir śaiva loci (spanda, śiva sūtra, pratyabhijñāhṛdaya, ipk).md
thinkers.parts: His recognition is of the Lord; the book keeps recognition and releases the Lord.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/the kashmir shaiva tradition would decline four of the book's deepest moves.md

thinkers.name: Abhinavagupta
thinkers.quote: the means where there is nothing to be done
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — abhinavagupta on the anupaya (the no-means).md
thinkers.parts: He reserves the no-means for the most graced; the book offers it to every reader.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — abhinavagupta on the anupaya (the no-means).md

thinkers.name: Kṣemarāja
thinkers.quote: this Self's assumed roles accepted of his own accord like the roles accepted by an actor
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — bhartṛhari's levels of speech and kṣemarāja on saṅkoca (vākyapadīya i; pratyabhijñāhṛdayam).md
thinkers.parts: He explains contraction's mechanism but withholds the book's praise of the limited standpoint.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — bhartṛhari's levels of speech and kṣemarāja on saṅkoca (vākyapadīya i; pratyabhijñāhṛdayam).md

thinkers.name: al-Junayd of Baghdad
thinkers.quote: Sufism means that God causes you to die for yourself, while endowing you with a life in Him
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — al-junayd and al-qushayri on fana and baqa.md
thinkers.parts: His return is subsistence in God, a destination the book's psychological register cannot assume.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — al-junayd and al-qushayri on fana and baqa.md

thinkers.name: al-Qushayrī
thinkers.quote: States come without asking, whereas stations are acquired by the sweat of one's brow.
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — al-qushayri, the risala on state and station (knysh 2007).md
thinkers.parts: He requires a master for a novice's formation; a book read alone cannot supply one.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/al-qushayri.md

thinkers.name: Dōgen
thinkers.quote: Because practice within realization occurs at the moment of practice, the practice of beginner's mind is itself the entire original realization
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — dogen, bendowa on shusho itto (c. 1231).md
thinkers.parts: His practice has no goal; the book promises transformation and an arc toward a peak.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — dogen, bendowa on shusho itto (c. 1231).md

thinkers.name: Ignatius of Loyola
thinkers.quote: it is not much knowledge that fills and satisfies the soul, but the intimate understanding and relish of the truth
thinkers.quote_src: notes/ignatius of loyola.md
thinkers.parts: His companion is forbidden to persuade; the book's own voice persuades by design.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/ignatius of loyola.md

thinkers.name: William James
thinkers.quote: I cannot impart acquaintance with them to any one who has not already made it himself.
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — james, the principles of psychology (1890).md
thinkers.parts: He judges an experience by its fruits in a life, not by a felt shift.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/william james.md

thinkers.name: Martin Buber
thinkers.quote: Through the Thou a man becomes I
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — buber, i and thou and elements of the interhuman (1923, 1965).md
thinkers.parts: A curriculum held as a means turns the meeting into an It.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/martin buber.md

thinkers.name: Martin Heidegger
thinkers.quote: making manifest that which in some sense lies hidden
thinkers.quote_src: notes/aletheia and pratyabhijna converge on truth as un-forgetting.md
thinkers.parts: Unconcealment is an event of Being, not a felt arrival in a reader.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/martin heidegger.md

thinkers.name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
thinkers.quote: The aspects of things that are most important for us are hidden because of their simplicity and familiarity.
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — wittgenstein (investigations, tractatus, on certainty).md
thinkers.parts: For him noticing dissolves a false problem; for the book it discloses what was there.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/ludwig wittgenstein.md

thinkers.name: Simone Weil
thinkers.quote: In a sense God renounces being everything. We should renounce being something.
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — weil, gravity and grace on decreation (1947).md
thinkers.parts: She un-creates the self to make room for God; the book restores the first person.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — weil, gravity and grace on decreation (1947).md

thinkers.name: Maurice Merleau-Ponty
thinkers.quote: One's own body is in the world just as the heart is in the organism
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — merleau-ponty, phenomenology of perception on the body-subject (1945).md
thinkers.parts: His body is the perceiver itself, not an instrument that certifies a felt shift.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/maurice merleau-ponty.md

thinkers.name: Carl Rogers
thinkers.quote: the techniques of the various therapies are relatively unimportant except to the extent that they serve as channels for fulfilling one of the conditions
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — rogers, the necessary and sufficient conditions (1957).md
thinkers.parts: Read alone, the book cannot offer the perceived relationship his conditions require.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/carl rogers.md

thinkers.name: Donald Winnicott
thinkers.quote: the basis of the capacity to be alone is a paradox; it is the experience of being alone while someone else is present
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — winnicott, the four moves kept distinct (1958–1971).md
thinkers.parts: A book cannot survive destruction or adapt, so it cannot be a live other.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — winnicott, the four moves kept distinct (1958–1971).md

thinkers.name: Eugene Gendlin
thinkers.quote: Not even the individual himself judges it but, we might say somewhat poetically, his direct referent does the judging
thinkers.quote_src: notes/eugene gendlin.md
thinkers.parts: The shift certifies that the process carried forward, not that a content is true.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/eugene gendlin.md

thinkers.name: Michael Polanyi
thinkers.quote: I shall reconsider human knowledge by starting from the fact that we can know more than we can tell
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — polanyi, the tacit dimension (1966).md
thinkers.parts: Attending to what you dwell in dissolves it; the book attends to the felt shift.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — polanyi, the tacit dimension (1966).md

thinkers.name: Kurt Lewin
thinkers.place: Cambridge, Massachusetts; workshop at New Britain, Connecticut
thinkers.quote: Research that produces nothing but books will not suffice
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — the facilitated room's roots (lewin 1946, johnstone's impro).md
thinkers.parts: His claim is knowing by intervening, not the intervener being remade.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — the facilitated room's roots (lewin 1946, johnstone's impro).md

thinkers.name: Werner Erhard
thinkers.quote: When a context uses you, there is nothing to remember and no rules to apply.
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — erhard and jensen, creating leaders (2010, rev. 2020).md
thinkers.parts: His course has students create a context; the book lets what is already there show.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/erhard and the book take different verbs from the same heideggerian object.md

thinkers.name: Keith Johnstone
thinkers.quote: In reality status transactions continue all the time
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — the facilitated room's roots (lewin 1946, johnstone's impro).md
thinkers.parts: Nothing in his method survives a person working alone with a book.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/keith johnstone.md

thinkers.name: Humberto Maturana and Francisco Varela
thinkers.quote: the living being is a source of perturbations and not of instructions
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — the participation law's independent arrivals (von foerster, maturana-varela, garfinkel, schön, de jaegher-di paolo, vervaeke).md
thinkers.parts: No text installs anything, this book included; it can only perturb.
thinkers.parts_src: notes/maturana and varela.md

thinkers.name: Karla McLaren
thinkers.quote: neither approach works because neither one accepts emotions as important messengers
thinkers.quote_src: archive/reading — the completion family (hudson's art of accomplishment, mclaren's language of emotions).md
thinkers.parts: She says grief can complete alone; the book holds grief needs a witness.
thinkers.parts_src: archive/reading — the completion family (hudson's art of accomplishment, mclaren's language of emotions).md

relations.note: Heidegger quoted Laozi on the Way and began translating the Daodejing, 1946.
relations.src: notes/heidegger's letting and way descend from daoism so pairing him with laozi is lineage not convergence.md

relations.note: Heidegger read Buber's 1910 Zhuangzi selection by 1930; which passages is unconfirmed.
relations.src: archive/reading — zhuangzi (wu-wei, the fasting of the mind, and sitting in forgetting).md

relations.note: Heidegger's Parmenides lectures place forgetting inside the remembering line from Plato.
No channel from Heidegger to Kashmir Śaivism; un-concealment and recognition arose separately.
relations.src: archive/reading — reinhard may, heidegger's hidden sources (1996).md

relations.note: One sympathetic 1929 remark is the only contact; nothing descends into §129.
Buber reached I and Thou independently of Heidegger, then argued against him.
Erhard cites Being and Time by page and builds on Heidegger's clearing.
relations.src: archive/reading — erhard and jensen, creating leaders (2010, rev. 2020).md

relations.note: Merleau-Ponty inherits phenomenological method, then departs from Heidegger's bodiless Dasein.
est descends from Lewin's T-group through the encounter movement: one lineage, not two arrivals.
relations.src: archive/reading — the facilitated room's roots (lewin 1946, johnstone's impro).md

relations.note: Both draw on Gestalt psychology, so they are not two independent roads.
Gendlin's felt-shift research ran in Rogers's Chicago center and Wisconsin project.
Abhinavagupta commented on Utpaladeva and developed his idea of wonder (camatkāra).
relations.src: archive/reading — the kashmir śaiva loci (spanda, śiva sūtra, pratyabhijñāhṛdaya, ipk).md

relations.note: Kṣemarāja was Abhinavagupta's disciple and condensed the recognition school's teaching.
The Kashmir school took his three levels of speech and added a fourth.
relations.src: archive/reading — bhartṛhari's levels of speech and kṣemarāja on saṅkoca (vākyapadīya i; pratyabhijñāhṛdayam).md

relations.note: Qushayrī's Risāla quotes Junayd and teaches his sober path of return.
relations.src: archive/reading — al-junayd and al-qushayri on fana and baqa.md

relations.note: Śaṅkara refuted emptiness by name; rivals charged Advaita with Madhyamaka borrowing.
